newsitem.title: GUATEMALA: Central America discusses regional power system.
newsitem.headline: Central America discusses regional power system.

text.p: Central American energy ministers were due to meet here Wednesday to discuss linking up electricity systems from Guatemala to Panama, officials said on Wednesday.

"The Central American ministers will adopt actions having to do with the Central American Electricity Interconnection System," Leonel Lopez, Guatemala's Energy Minister, said in a press release on Wednesday.
The seven Central American nations plan to create a multinational company which will develop, design, finance, construct and maintain a regional network connecting their electric systems.
Supporters of the project say they hope to have the network functioning within five years, and that it will bring consumer electric prices in the region down by ten percent.
Ministers will also review a report from a regional energy commission and discuss promoting investment in oil exploration in the region.

The energy ministers from Guatemala, Belize, Honduras, Nicaragua, El Salvador, Costa Rica, and Panama are here as part of a larger conference, the twenty-seventh meeting of Latin American energy ministers slated to begin here Thursday.
The Latin American ministers will look at promoting private investment in energy projects and at sharing technical and financial assistance throughout the region.
